title: B.C. police watchdog clears officers in 3 incidents
subtitle: The Independent Investigations Office investigated three incidents in late 2012
article: Police officers involved in three separate incidents did not commit any offences, according to the province's police watchdog.
The Independent Investigations Office (IIO) was called in to investigate three incidents in November and December of 2012.

The first incident occurred on Nov. 13, 2012 when Vancouver police used a Taser on a distraught man after he had repeatedly stabbed himself outside of his home in East Vancouver. Alton Cuyugan was taken into custody and transported to hospital where he later died.

The second incident occurred on Dec. 21, 2012 when a man was stopped by Surrey RCMP officers at King George Boulevard 24th Avenue. The man turned a gun on himself before he was taken into custody and transported to hospital where he died of his injuries.

The third incident occurred on Dec. 27, 2012 when an on-duty RCMP officer driving an unmarked police passenger van collided with a male driver at the intersection of Highway 10 and 184th Street in Surrey.

The man suffered fractured ribs and lacerations to his lung. Although the injuries were not believed to be life-threatening at the time, the driver later died in hospital after his condition continued to deteriorate.
The IIO found that the driver was distracted by an oncoming ambulance and had made a sudden left turn in front of the RCMP officer's vehicle, resulting in the crash.
Following three investigations, Chief Civilian Director Richard Rosenthal concluded that there was no evidence that any police officer committed an offence related to the deaths.
